papers.title: Operator Algebras and Their Applications
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of commutative associative algebras whose structural constants are linear operators acting in a linear topological space. An analogue of the theory of monogenic functions is developed for such algebras. It is shown that the components of monogenic functions satisfy second-order operator-differential equations. This approach provides a constructive method for obtaining solutions of various partial differential and integro-differential equations. Several illustrative examples are presented.

papers.title: Hsiang cubics as spherical Chebyshev polynomials: equioscillation and idempotent quadrature
papers.abstract: A Hsiang cubic is a cubic form on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose zero set is a minimal cone; equivalently, it is the cubic form of a commutative nonassociative metrized algebra satisfying a single identity of degree four. We show that the intrinsic geometry of such an algebra, encoded in its idempotents and their Peirce decompositions, is the geometry of a Chebyshev-type extremal problem on the sphere. A Hsiang cubic equioscillates on $S^{n-1}$: its maximum set is the set of normalized idempotents, and on suitable great circles through an idempotent it restricts to the Chebyshev polynomial $T_3$. For the spherical analogue of the problem of least deviation, the minimization of $\|p\|_\infty^2/\|p\|_2^2$ over harmonic cubics, a sharp lower bound based on Kellogg's inequality shows that Cartan's isoparametric cubics are the global minimizers in dimensions $5$, $8$, $14$ and $26$. In general, we compute the ratio of every Hsiang cubic in terms of the Killing form and characterize stationarity by a Kolmogorov criterion: it amounts to a positive measure on the idempotent variety. Such measures are given explicitly in several cases which together cover every Hsiang cubic known to exist; in particular, all of them are stationary. These measures give quadrature identities on the idempotent variety whose moments are invariants of the algebra; they are spherical designs exactly in the Einstein (Killing metrized) case, i.e.\ when the Killing form is proportional to the inner product. Distinguished low-dimensional Hsiang cubics are strict local minimizers, whereas a polar Hsiang cubic is a stationary non-minimizer.

papers.title: Products of Boolean Clones up to Minion Homomorphisms
papers.abstract: We study the minion homomorphism poset of multisorted Boolean clones. Our main result completely determines the subposet induced by products of Boolean clones: every inequality between prod- ucts is induced by inequalities between their Boolean factors. Furthermore, we determine the minion cores of all products of Boolean clones, thereby identifying canonical representatives of their minion homomorphic equivalence classes.

papers.title: Homogeneous symmetric trace-positive sextics with vanishing abelianization are sums of Hermitian squares and commutators
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}\langle X,Y\rangle$ be the free algebra on two symmetric letters. A polynomial is trace-positive if it has non-negative trace on every pair of real symmetric matrices, and it lies in the cone $\Theta$ if it is cyclically equivalent to a sum of Hermitian squares. Burgdorf and Klep proved that the two notions coincide in degree at most four; from degree six onwards they differ. We give a complete, explicit description of both cones on the six-dimensional space $Z$ of symmetric homogeneous sextics in two symmetric letters whose abelianization vanishes identically, and show that on $Z$ they coincide: for $f\in Z$, trace-positivity is equivalent to membership in $\Theta_3$, to non-negativity of the trace on pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices, and to being cyclically equivalent to a sum of four Hermitian squares of cubics with vanishing abelianization. Membership in $\Theta$ reduces to a $4\times4$ positive semidefinite Gram matrix whose diagonal blocks are fixed by the content-$(4,2)$ and $(2,4)$ parts of $f$; each of those parts ranges over a two-dimensional cone with two linear facets, and the content-$(3,3)$ part is then confined to a rectangle whose sides are the geometric means $\sqrt{p_+q_+}$ and $\sqrt{p_-q_-}$ of the eigenvalues of those blocks. Each facet is certified by one of two families of pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices. The abelianization hypothesis is natural: every bivariate degree-six example we are aware of -- a trace-positive polynomial outside $\Theta$ -- arises by lifting a non-negative, non-SOS polynomial in two variables to a cyclically sorted polynomial; and that lifting cannot operate when the abelianization vanishes. Symmetry of $f$ is essential: dropping it adds one antisymmetric direction, on which the trace vanishes identically, yet whose non-zero elements all lie outside $\Theta$.

papers.title: The finite basis problem for varieties generated by all semirings of a fixed order
papers.abstract: Let $\Avar_n$ and $\VV_n$ be the varieties generated by all $n$-element additively idempotent semirings (ai-semirings) and all $n$-element semirings with commutative addition, respectively, in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without constants. We prove that both varieties are finitely based if and only if $n\leq2$. The five-element case follows from cyclic identities and a structural analysis of products of squares. For $n\geq6$, each variety contains a finite inherently nonfinitely based ai-semiring. We also prove $\VV_n\cap\AI=\Avar_n$ for every $n$, where $\AI$ is the variety of all ai-semirings.

papers.title: The six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based
papers.abstract: We show that the six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based. More precisely, for every positive integer $n$, we construct an infinite additively idempotent semiring, generated by at most $(6n+8)^2$ elements, that satisfies every $n$-variable identity of $B_2^1$.

papers.title: A unified approach to the definition of anti-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the $\mathfrak M$arseille anti-construction $\mathfrak{Ma}$ for varieties of algebras defined by multilinear identities of degree $3$, obtained by changing the sign of the right-nested part of each defining polynomial. This gives, for any variety $\Var$, a new variety $\mathfrak{Ma}$-$\Var$ that generalizes antiassociative algebras and the recently studied anti-Novikov and anti-right-symmetric $\big($pre-Jacobi--Jordan$\big)$ algebras. We describe free objects in several $\mathfrak{Ma}$-varieties. On the operadic level, over a field of characteristic $\mathrm{char}\,\Bbbk\neq 2$, we show $(\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}\Var)^{(!)}=\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}(\Var^{(!)})$ and that the Dong property is preserved by $\mathfrak{Ma}.$ Finally, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition for $\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}\Var=\Var$. The second part of the paper is dedicated to another type of anti-algebras, called $\mathcal{M}anin$ anti-algebras. We give the description of this type of algebras via calculation of the white Manin product of suitable operads and present various examples of known $\mathcal{M}anin$ anti-algebras. In the end, we proved that the symmetric affinization of an algebra gives a Jacobi-Jordan algebra if and only if the original algebra is a $\mathcal{M}a$-Novikov algebra, that is, an analog of a well-known result about affinization of Novikov algebras given by Balinskii and Novikov.

papers.title: Quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$
papers.abstract: We compute quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$. In particular, we prove that $\mathcal{B}(q)$ has various nontrivial quasi-derivations, i.e., quasi-derivations different from derivations and $\delta$-derivations. As corollaries, we have the complete description of $\delta$-derivations, $\delta$-biderivations, and transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures on $\mathcal{B}(q)$. In particular, $\mathcal{B}(q),$ up to isomorphisms, admits only one nontrivial transposed $\delta$-Poisson structure if $q\in \mathbb Z$ and $\mathcal{B}(q)$ does not admits nontrivial transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures if $q\notin \mathbb Z.$

papers.title: Non-Existence of Abelian KS-Algebras in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ for $n \geq 3$
papers.abstract: We prove that $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ contains no abelian Kadison--Singer algebra for any $n \geq 3$.

papers.title: Complex slices, inverses, and deformations of a three-dimensional real algebra
papers.abstract: We study the real three-dimensional unital algebra with basis $\{1,i,j\}$ and products $i^2=j^2=-1,\quad ij=0,\quad ji=i+j$. Its quadratic and power-associative elements form the union of exactly three complex subalgebras; their nonzero elements are precisely those with a two-sided inverse, which is unique. Every nonzero subalgebra contains the unit, and every element outside these three planes generates the whole algebra. We classify one-sided inverses, including the singular cases, and show that two-sided invertibility does not imply cancellation. The multiplication algebra is $M_3(\mathbb{R})$, so the algebra is absolutely central simple. Its derivations vanish, its automorphism group is trivial, and its commutator Lie algebra is $\mathbb{R}\oplus\mathfrak{aff}(1)$. Its unique antiautomorphism is involutive, and its complexification admits no complex-linear structurable involution. Finally, replacing $ji=i+j$ by $ji=t(i+j)$ gives real algebras $\mathcal{A}_t$ with $\mathcal{A}_s\cong\mathcal{A}_t$ exactly when $s^2=t^2$. We describe the exceptional parameters and thereby exhibit nontrivial deformations of the original algebra.

papers.title: On the non-existence of a left-symmetric structure on osp(1|2) in any characteristic
papers.abstract: Burde proved that the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of characteristic $p > 2$, admits compatible left-symmetric algebra structures if and only if $p = 3$. Since the even part of the Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, we ask whether Burde's structures can be extended to compatible left-symmetric superalgebra structures on $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$. We verify Burde's left-symmetric structures on $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, and then test their possible extensions to $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$. We show that no such extension exists in characteristic 3. Together with the obstruction coming from the even part for characteristic $0$ and $p > 3$, this gives non-existence for a field $\mathbb{K}$ of characteristic different from $2$.

papers.title: Global obstruction property and its applications
papers.abstract: We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite. For each Artin algebra $A$, we construct an algebra $\mathcal{G}(A)$ satisfying GOP by using triangular matrix extensions. We show that $\text{fin.dim}\mathcal{G}(A)=\text{fin.dim} A+2$ and that $A$ and $\mathcal{G}(A)$ are singularly equivalent. Finally, we give a pair of derived equivalent finite-dimensional algebras for which GOP holds on only one side.

papers.title: Projective Differential Moment Invariants from the Viewpoint of Classical Invariant Theory
papers.abstract: Polynomial first-order projective differential moment invariants are investigated. The main result establishes an exact correspondence between such moment invariants and symmetric polynomial multipoint relative projective differential invariants of weight $-1$. This correspondence describes each homogeneous component with respect to moment degree and allows previously obtained results on relative projective invariants to be used for systematic construction. It is also proved that passing from the formal algebra of moments to their integral definitions introduces no additional algebraic relations among the constructed invariants. For low moment degrees, the absence of nontrivial invariants of degrees $1$ and $2$ is established, and a complete description of degree $3$ invariants is obtained. The ten cubic differential moments are naturally identified with the coefficients of a ternary cubic, connecting the construction with classical invariant theory. In particular, the Aronhold invariants $S$ and $T$ yield projective differential moment invariants of degrees $4$ and $6$. One of the known moment invariants of Wang et al. is shown to be proportional to $S$. The algebra of polynomial moment invariants is proved not to be finitely generated. The field of rational moment invariants coincides with the field of fractions of the polynomial invariant algebra. For the explicit constructions, compact multipoint representations define the corresponding moment polynomials without requiring their full expansions. These representations provide a basis for algorithmic construction and software computation of the invariants.

papers.title: A 9-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to its complex conjugate admitting no real form
papers.abstract: We give an explicit example of a 9-dimensional 5-step nilpotent complex Lie algebra, generated by two elements, that is isomorphic to its complex conjugate but has no real form. In contrast to the earlier 10-dimensional examples, our proof is completely elementary and very short.

papers.title: The $E_6$ normal forms: semisimple deformations, geometry, DT invariants, and the $E_{6,\infty}$ order
papers.abstract: We study the completed Jacobi algebras of $x^3+xy^3+p(y)$ for $\operatorname{ord}_yp=n\ge4$. The explicit normal-form morsification, the filtered length and centre proofs, and the cyclic terminal identities give finite free semisimple deformations. For every parameter of finite order we construct a polynomial curve neighbourhood and a local projective small contraction; the resulting geometric GV and Donaldson--Thomas calculations identify the block multiplicities. The one-dimensional limit $E_{6,\infty}$ is studied separately as an order: we determine its normalization, conductor, radical-idealizer chain, and maximal overorders. The canonical chain yields a nine-dimensional finite quotient whose Ringel dual is isomorphic to its opposite. An expanded construction gives a choice-independent $22$-dimensional quotient and a $40$-dimensional Ringel dual; a corner quotient relates the two finite constructions. The length and centre formulas are proved by a filtered comparison with a homogeneous matrix order and by terminal identities at the exceptional endpoint.

papers.title: Jacobson radicals of Ore extensions
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a ring, $\sigma$ be an automorphism of $R$, and $D$ be a $\sigma$-derivation on $R$ with $D\sigma=\sigma D$. We will show that $J(R[x;\sigma,D])\subseteq A[x;\sigma,D]$ where $A$ is a collection of all leading coefficients of polynomials in $J(R[x;\sigma,D])$. In addition, we will prove that $J(R[x;\sigma,D])\cap R$ is nil if $\sigma$ is locally torsion and one of the following conditions is given: (1) $R$ is a PI-ring and $D$ is $q$-skew, (2) $R$ is an algebra over a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $D$ is a locally nilpotent derivation such that $\sigma D=D\sigma$. This answers partially an open question by Greenfeld, Smoktunowicz and Ziembowski.

papers.title: Right representations of Novikov algebras
papers.abstract: We study the theory of right representations of Novikov algebras. We introduce the notion of a modular right ideal of a Novikov algebra and prove that every irreducible right representation of a Novikov algebra is isomorphic to the quotient by a maximal modular right ideal. We prove that the class of Novikov algebras with no irreducible representations forms a hereditary radical. We introduce the notion of a primitive Novikov algebra and show that a Novikov algebra is primitive if and only if it admits an almost faithful irreducible representation. We also introduce the notion of the quasi-kernel of a representation, defined as the largest ideal contained in its kernel. Finally, we prove that the constructed radical coincides with the intersection of the quasi-kernels of all its irreducible representations.
